`UnifiedActivationPipeline` (`.aios-core/development/scripts/unified-activation-pipeline.js`) is the single entry point for all 12 agents; `generate-greeting.js` delegates to `UnifiedActivationPipeline.activate(agentId)`. `GreetingBuilder` assembles greetings from pipeline-preloaded enriched context. `loadUserProfile()` runs in `buildGreeting()` and passes to `_buildContextualGreeting()` to avoid duplicate `resolveConfig()` calls. `GreetingPreferenceManager.getPreference(userProfile)` accepts optional userProfile for bob-mode restriction. PM bypasses bob restriction (primary bob interface); non-PM bob agents: preference `auto` shows redirect, forced `named` shows simple named greeting; bob non-PM commands are empty. Phases: 1) five parallel loaders (`Promise.all`); 2) agent definition; 3) sequential preference/session type/workflow; 4) enriched context; 5) GreetingBuilder.

Eight agents have command `visibility: [full, quick, key]`; `qa`, `data-engineer`, `devops`, `ux-design-expert` lack visibility and fall back to first 12 commands. `aios-master` uses `visibility: full`. `*yolo` is universal across 12 agents. Badge: `_safeGetPermissionBadge()` in greeting-builder.js. Formats: structured (`name: xxx`) and compact (`key: 'value'`); compact agents: qa, devops, data-engineer, ux-design-expert. Match existing format when editing. Sources: `.aios-core/development/agents/`; Claude mirror: `.claude/commands/AIOS/agents/`. Separate files; `ideSync` handles sync.

`resolveConfig()` merges L1-L5; L5 (`user-config.yaml`) highest priority. `user_profile` is USER_FIELD in migrate-config.js; `toggleUserProfile()` in config-resolver.js flips bob<->advanced. `validate-user-profile.js` `validateUserProfile()` is pure (no filesystem), usable without test mocking.

Always mock `fs`, `js-yaml`, `config-resolver`, and dependency modules BEFORE requiring the module under test. Mock `resolveConfig` with `mockReturnValue` (not `mockReturnValueOnce`) when called multiple times. Double `loadUserProfile()` broke tests using `mockReturnValueOnce`. `jest.clearAllMocks()` does NOT reset `mockImplementation()` -- only clears call history. If tests override `mockImplementation`, subsequent tests inherit the override. Fix: explicitly restore default mock implementations in `beforeEach`, or use `jest.restoreAllMocks()` (which only works with `jest.spyOn`). For `jest.mock()` factories, must manually re-apply defaults. Changed mock constructors (e.g., `AgentConfigLoader.mockImplementation(...)`): `beforeEach` pipeline construction uses the active mock; runtime calls (e.g., `new SessionContextLoader()`) use the CURRENT mock. `jest.mock()` is hoisted; cannot use `path.resolve()` in its mock path argument before `const path = require('path')`. `console.warn` template literal is one argument; match with `stringContaining()` only. Existing `greeting-builder.test.js` globally mocks GreetingPreferenceManager to return `auto`, so bob mode falls through to contextual redirect logic. Use `jest.requireActual('fs')` for real filesystem checks in hook existence tests. Use `os.tmpdir()` with unique suffixes for test temp dirs; cleanup with `fs.rmSync`. Do not mock `child_process.execSync` as `execa`; they are different modules. When `writeFile` serves lock+cache, use broad `mockResolvedValue`; verify via `mock.calls` filtering.

Use `fs.writeFile(path, data, { flag: 'wx' })` for exclusive create lock; simpler/more testable than `fs.open('wx')`. Include PID + timestamp for stale detection; threshold ~10s, timeout ~3s, poll every 50ms. Temp file `{path}.tmp.{pid}` + `fs.rename()`; Windows rename fails if target exists, so fall back to direct `fs.writeFile()`. Cache fingerprint: `.git/HEAD` mtime + `.git/index` mtime.
